exclude: What must you get in writing?

questions.q: An author previewed a page, and a stakeholder says the public site still shows the old text. What is the most likely reason?
options: The page was previewed but not published
Code Sync has failed, so the published version is waiting for a deployment
The sitemap is out of date
questions.explain: Preview updates aem.page. Publishing updates aem.live and purges the production CDN.

questions.q: A developer loads a large marketing tag in the eager phase, and LCP gets worse. Where should the tag load?
options: After the page content, in the delayed phase
In head.html, before aem.js, so that it can track the first paint
questions.explain: Eager is for what LCP needs. Third-party work should come last.

questions.q: A small team lives in Word and SharePoint, and wants to start quickly. Which authoring options best fit their skills?
options: A custom headless CMS with a React front end deployed through a bundler
questions.explain: Match the authoring option to the people who will use it.

questions.q: An author pastes a table to create a three-column layout, but its first row says “Columns (3)” in plain text outside the table. What happens?
options: The text is treated as content, and the table will not be the named block
EDS infers the block from the number of columns, and still decorates it as Columns
questions.explain: The block name belongs in the first row of the table.

questions.q: Two sections on a page need different background colours. What should the author use?
options: A section break and Section Metadata
A new block for each colour, with the colour as its name
questions.explain: Sections group content, and Section Metadata can apply a style.

questions.q: An author wants a page title and description for search results. Where do they go?
options: The Metadata block on that page
The first paragraph, which EDS sends to search engines as the title
questions.explain: Page metadata belongs in the Metadata block.

questions.q: A developer runs aem up and sees the old site content but new code. What does this tell you?
options: The CLI serves local code with remote content
Local code only takes effect once a page is previewed from Sidekick
questions.explain: The local proxy serves your code and fetches content from the project.

questions.q: A hero image is the largest element, but it loads lazily. What should change?
options: Load it eagerly, as it is the LCP candidate
Convert it to a CSS background, so it loads before the HTML is parsed
questions.explain: The LCP image must not wait.

questions.q: A block’s CSS accidentally styles links across the whole page. What should the developer do?
options: Scope selectors to the block’s class
Add more !important rules in styles.css, so the page's links win
questions.explain: Block CSS should be scoped to that block.

questions.q: A new block named “price table” does not load its code. What should the folder be called?
questions.explain: Block names become lowercase, dash-separated folder names.

questions.q: A page must stay published but must never appear in search results. What should you set?
options: Disallow its URL in robots.txt and nothing else
questions.explain: Crawlers must be able to read the page to see noindex.

questions.q: Every page in /news needs one template. What is the best tool?
options: Bulk metadata with a URL pattern
A custom block per page, with the template name in its table
questions.explain: The metadata sheet applies values by URL pattern.

questions.q: Editors need to reuse one promotion on 40 pages and change it in one place. What should they use?
questions.explain: A fragment is authored once and included on many pages.

questions.q: A new project has no existing authoring system, and wants Adobe’s recommended default. What should it choose?
questions.explain: aem.live calls it the recommended default content source for new projects.

questions.q: In Universal Editor, authors can add any block to any section, which is causing layouts to break. What should a developer change?
options: A rule in the CDN configuration for each section
questions.explain: Filters control what can be added to a container.

questions.q: Fonts load late, and text jumps when they arrive. What helps most?
options: Removing all headings until the web font has finished loading
questions.explain: Matching metrics reduces layout shift.

questions.q: A blog listing must filter posts by tag across thousands of pages. What should you use?
options: A query index with the needed columns
A hand-maintained list in the nav, updated by an author after each post
questions.explain: Add tags to the index, and request only what you need.

questions.q: A branch URL does not resolve. Its combined name is 71 characters. What is wrong?
options: It exceeds the 63-character DNS label limit
The branch has no README, so Code Sync has not created a URL for it
questions.explain: ref--site--org must fit in one label.

questions.q: A team wants a shared staging branch because “that is how we always did it”, with no complex CDN logic. What do you recommend?
options: Use feature branches with protected main
Add a long-lived staging branch, with its own CDN and release schedule
questions.explain: Each branch is already an environment.

questions.q: A launch needs hreflang for English and French. Where does AEM support it directly?
options: In a Sidekick plugin that adds the links after publishing
questions.explain: Each language can set hreflang and alternate.

questions.q: A live site must move to a new content source. What is the recommended path?
options: Create a new site, validate it, and switch the CDN origin
Change content.source on the live site
Delete and recreate the site in place during a low-traffic window, then republish all pages
questions.explain: Changing it in place creates a new Content Bus ID.

questions.q: Production stays stale after a publish, while aem.live shows the new page. What do you check?
options: Push invalidation configuration and its opt-in header
Whether the page has an h1, because the CDN skips pages without one
questions.explain: aem.live is correct, so the production CDN is not being purged.

questions.q: After enabling a BYO CDN, identical URLs with different query strings return the same response. What is wrong?
options: Query parameters are not in the cache key
HSTS is on, so the CDN strips the query string from each request
questions.explain: Query parameters must be forwarded and included in the cache key.

questions.q: A site’s origin is protected and visitors now get 401 through the CDN. What is missing?
options: The CDN must send a site token
A new sitemap listing the protected paths for the CDN
questions.explain: The CDN needs the Authorization header on origin requests.

questions.q: A team adds a nonce-based CSP, and block scripts stop loading. Which part is probably missing?
questions.explain: 'strict-dynamic' lets trusted scripts load others.

questions.q: A stakeholder asks for every retired URL to redirect to the home page. What should you recommend?
options: Redirect valuable URLs to relevant pages, and let the rest return 404
Redirect them all, since one wildcard keeps the link value of every retired URL and avoids any 404s
Use a wildcard in the sheet
questions.explain: Base redirects on real use.

questions.q: A filtered telemetry view looks much worse than last week. What should you check first?
options: The sample size and margin of error
The Git history of the blocks changed in the last week
The number of authors active this week
questions.explain: Filtering shrinks the sample and increases uncertainty.

questions.q: An analytics tag must not run before consent. Where does it belong?
options: Behind consent, in the delayed phase
In a public configuration value read by scripts.js
questions.explain: Respect consent, and keep third parties late.

questions.q: A script receives 429 while publishing pages. What should it do?
options: Retry at once in a loop
Use more IP addresses, so that the limit applies to each one
questions.explain: 429 means rate limited.

questions.q: Estimated views are 30,000 per variant, at a sample weight of 100, and conversions differ slightly. Why can you not trust the result yet?
options: Only about 300 views per variant were sampled
Estimates are exact, so the test has already reached its required sample
questions.explain: Significance depends on sampled counts.

questions.q: A portfolio has 14 white-label brands that must not expose each other’s design tokens. Which approach fits?
options: Repoless with separate theme files loaded by metadata
One CSS file with all brand tokens
A repository copy per brand, kept in sync by hand through a monthly merge
questions.explain: Shared CSS makes every brand visible to every visitor.

questions.q: Half a site stays on AEM publish during a staged move. What keeps visitors on one domain?
options: A browser redirect on every page
A second domain with a banner
questions.explain: The CDN can route paths to each origin.

questions.q: Three teams each built a carousel. What should governance add first?
options: A block catalog with owners and a reuse check
A rule that each team must keep its own copy of every block
questions.explain: Check for reuse before building.

questions.q: A decision has three people marked Accountable, and nothing gets done. What should change?
options: Remove the RACI, and let the three people agree between themselves
questions.explain: Shared accountability often means none.

questions.q: Target runs on every page for one home-page banner, and mobile LCP has risen. What should you do?
options: Limit it to the pages that need it, using a metadata flag
Add it to head.html, so the Target library is cached before the home page is reached
questions.explain: Adobe advises enabling it only on selected pages.

questions.q: A team proposes prerendering all two million SKUs for SEO. What should guide the decision?
options: Crawl demand and Search Console data
The SKU count alone, as every product needs a prerendered page
questions.explain: Crawl demand sets the useful number of pages.

questions.q: A form’s Rule Editor hides a field, and someone posts it directly. What protects the data?
options: The client-side rule, as hidden fields are never submitted
questions.explain: Browser rules are not a control.

questions.q: An AI assistant will change 2,000 pages. What is the safest way to begin?
options: Propose changes for a small sample, then have a person review them
Let it publish all 2,000 in batches, and only check those that a person flags afterward
questions.explain: Start small, and keep a human in charge.

questions.q: A team needs a new action in the Universal Editor properties panel. What should it build?
options: A UI extension with App Builder
A metadata sheet with one row for each action
questions.explain: Universal Editor extensions use App Builder.

questions.q: Budget allows fixing one site. Site A has LCP 4 s and 5,000 views, and Site B has LCP 2.8 s and 3 million views. Where do you usually begin?
options: Site B, as more visitors are affected
Site A, since its LCP is the further from the good threshold
The one with the shortest name
questions.explain: Weigh severity with reach.

questions.q: A customer wants a fast marketing site and already owns complex AEM workflows. What is the first question to settle?
options: Which authoring model and workflows must continue
Which front-end framework the current site's components use
questions.explain: Fit depends on people, process and constraints.

questions.q: Code on main changed, but a page still looks old on production. What are the first two things to separate? Choose the best.
options: Whether aem.live is new, and whether the production CDN is
Whether the author's document was saved after the last code merge to main
questions.explain: Check each tier in order to find where the old copy is.

questions.q: A brand refresh changes colours everywhere. What makes this a small change?
options: Design tokens as CSS custom properties
A separate CSS file per block and per brand colour, swapped in by metadata
questions.explain: One token change updates its users.

questions.q: A Universal Editor field should combine an image and its alt text in one element. Which feature applies?
questions.explain: Suffixes such as Alt combine properties.

questions.q: A pull request has failing PageSpeed checks, and a deadline looms. What should happen?
options: Fix it, or record an explicit exception by its owner
Disable the check for the whole repository until the release is over
questions.explain: Treat gates as gates.

questions.q: An image conveys a key instruction, and the author leaves alt text empty. What is the problem?
options: Screen reader users miss the information
Lighthouse fails the page, but readers lose nothing
The page fails to publish from Sidekick
The image is stretched to fill the empty alt space
questions.explain: Meaningful images need useful alt text.

questions.q: Translated pages keep drifting from their originals. What should the program define?
options: A source of truth, and a translation workflow
A weekly full re-translation of the whole site, without review
A separate site for each translator
questions.explain: Translation needs clear ownership.

questions.q: An author asks to A/B test a headline. Which is the right framing first?
options: A hypothesis, a primary metric and enough traffic
Change it for a week, then compare total sales with last week's numbers
Test ten headlines on a low-traffic page
questions.explain: Plan before you launch.

questions.q: A profile sets a security header, and one site removes it through its own configuration. Which applies?
questions.explain: The site wins conflicts.

questions.q: Two hours before launch, someone wants to change the code location. What should you do?
options: Stop it, and keep the configuration frozen
Do it, but purge everything first so the new location is used straight away
questions.explain: Adobe advises against late location changes.

questions.q: A leaked Admin API key is found in Git history. What is the right first action?
options: Revoke it, then review the audit log
Delete the line and move on
Make the repository private and keep the key
questions.explain: Treat it as compromised.

questions.q: A snapshot is approved while the code it needs has not merged. What should the team have done?
options: Publish the pages by hand, and add the code later in the day
questions.explain: Approving publishes the snapshot.

questions.q: After migration, organic traffic falls and Search Console reports many 404s. What is your first step?
options: Add redirects for valuable missing URLs
Reduce the sitemap to only those pages that still rank
questions.explain: Compare what is missing with real demand.

questions.q: Pages are generated from JSON, and a record is deleted at source. What must be planned?
options: A flow that unpublishes the page
Nothing, the page disappears with the next rebuild of the index
questions.explain: Generated pages stay live until removed.

questions.q: A designer proposes an auto-rotating six-slide hero. What do you raise?
options: Accessibility, LCP, and whether it is needed
Only the number of slides and the image file sizes, as rotation is a design choice
questions.explain: Motion needs pause controls, and carousels often hide content.

questions.q: You want to contribute a client’s block to open source. What comes first?
options: Remove client material, and confirm your rights
Rename the company in the code, then open a pull request straight away
questions.explain: Generalize it, and check permissions.
